newsitem.title: USA: Accused woman bomber asks for discharge - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Accused woman bomber asks for discharge - lawyer.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force's first woman B-52 pilot will ask superiors to be honorably discharged in order to avoid a court martial on a criminal charge of adultery, her lawyer said Saturday.

Frank Spinner, civilian attorney for Lt. Kelly Flinn, said in a statement that the request would likely be presented to the Air Force next week. Spinner said he was confident that the request would make its way through the chain of command and that Air Force Secretary Sheila Widnall would ultimately decide on the matter.

The pilot of heavy bombers, who is 26 and single, had been scheduled to be court-martialed on Tuesday at Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota, on charges of adultery and fraternization. She has acknowledged an affair with a married civilian and is also accused of having sex with a lower-ranking enlisted man.

In the statement, Flinn said her action would enable the Pentagon to continue to focus on appropriate and consistent ways to address gender issues in the military without the pressures of a protracted court-martial proceeding.
The statement said an honorable discharge would spare both her and the Air Force from further embarrassment over the issue.

Conviction of adultery in a military trial is punishable by penalties ranging up to dishonorable discharge and possible fines and imprisonment. Critics have argued that Flinn's case highlights a double standard in the way the U.S. Armed Forces treats the issue of adultery among its male and female staff.
